Root construction, synthesis, and executable contract
1 November 2026, Australia/Brisbane

What was strengthened
======================
MAIN_PROOF.txt first supplied the common stationary law and the target mass
and conditional sampler. The extension here earns those computational inputs
from local calibration for a restricted interacting model. It does not infer
an arbitrary physical mechanism. The pinned Astra N1213 acquisition ingredient
already learns local heatbath probabilities and compatible Ising weights;
this work credits and reuses that ingredient. The extension adds driven local
cycles, coarse targets, the joint weights/flows sensitivity proof, and the
screened mean and lifetime receiver. Standard inverse-Ising identification,
transfer matrices, Dobrushin coupling and potential theory remain its machinery.

An equally informed conventional method can adopt all these constructions.
No new universal feasibility class, strongest-method speed superiority or
historical priority has been established by this work.

1. A useful general sensitivity theorem
=======================================
Let L=-Q be a finite irreducible generator with positive unnormalized invariant
weights w. Write D=diag(w)L. The directed flows w(x)q_xy are balanced, so D has
zero row and column sums. Decompose this flow into positive directed cycle
coefficients c_j on a specified common cycle architecture. A cycle has length
at most ell. Its ordinary bilinear form B_j and energy E_j obey
   |B_j(f,h)| <= K sqrt(E_j(f) E_j(h)),   K=csc(pi/ell).
This follows from the Fourier modes of a cycle. Two- and three-cycles have
K=2/sqrt(3)<=7/6. This concerns STATIONARY-FLOW cycles; state-dependent accepted
moves need not themselves be permutation kernels.

Let the fitted model have weights what and coefficients chat_j, satisfying
   exp(-u) w <= what <= exp(u) w pointwise,
   exp(-v) c_j <= chat_j <= exp(v) c_j for every cycle.
For any nonempty proper target A, let M and Mhat be mean hitting times from
the respective stationary laws conditioned on B=A^c.

Thus

1 November 2026

RESULT

For a known binary path architecture, nonrare local clamping and marked unit
heatbath attempts acquire rational fitted factors and a simultaneous pointwise
stationary-weight confidence band. The true and fitted generators both have
an earned constant additive-symmetric gap. Directed local three-cycles can be
added with their stationary circulation explicitly constructed. No complete
rare target configuration is needed during calibration.

This is a model-qualified statistical construction, not a claim that arbitrary
physical clamping preserves native rates. The modular proposal/mark interface
below is essential. Standard logistic identification, transfer matrices and
Dobrushin coupling are credited as conventional machinery.

1. TRUE ARCHITECTURE AND ACTUALLY OBSERVED LOCAL INTERFACE

The state is x in {0,1}^n, n>=2. Unknown positive factors satisfy

   9/10 <= a_i,b_i <= 11/10,
   w(x)=product_(i=1)^n a_i^(x_i)
                   product_(i=1)^(n-1) b_i^(x_i x_(i+1)),
   pi(x)=w(x)/Z.

Each site has a visible independent unit-rate Poisson attempt clock. At an
attempt it proposes a heatbath redraw of x_i. Given its neighboring bits l,r,
the odds of a proposed1 versus0 are

   R_i(l,r)=a_i b_(i-1)^l b_i^r,

with missing boundary factors omitted. If the proposal equals the current bit,
the event is a marked null. The proposal probability does not depend on the
old bit. Proposal rates are a known local function of the displayed factors.

The calibration intervention may set/hold the current bit and its at most two
neighbors, and observe proposed redraw marks without committing them. Other
sites need not be prepared or frozen. Holding these local bits does not change
the proposal probabilities, attempt-clock rates or their readout convention.
This causal modularity follows from the declared proposal mechanism; it cannot
be inferred from finite unrestricted observations alone. If only state changes
are visible or a clamp changes the local proposal law, this protocol does not
apply without another paid observation/control construction.

Independent review, 2026-10-31. This note supplies caveats and an ordinary
construction, not a claim of a new feasibility class.

1. STRONG EQUALLY INFORMED ORDINARY CONSTRUCTION

For a binary path Gibbs model
  W(x)=exp(sum_i h_i x_i + sum_i J_i x_i x_{i+1}),  x_i in {-1,+1},
local heat-bath conditional probabilities satisfy
  (1/2)logit p_i(+|a,b)=h_i+J_{i-1}a+J_i b.
Holding the two neighbors in each of four contexts and observing marked
heat-bath update outcomes yields independent Bernoulli samples by the specified
heat-bath rule. The initial central spin and global mixing time are irrelevant.
Estimate conditional logits and use their four-point Walsh coefficients to
recover h_i and its incident J values. Average the two estimates of each shared
edge coupling. This ensures a compatible global Gibbs family; arbitrary
independently fitted conditional tables need not be compatible.

If all local conditional probabilities lie in [a,1-a], a>0, estimating each
probability to a*delta/2 is sufficient for parameter error at most delta (using
clipped estimates and a conservative logit derivative bound). Hoeffding gives
O(a^-2 delta^-2 log(n/alpha)) update attempts per local context. There are O(n)
contexts. To achieve uniform unnormalized log-weight error u it suffices to take
delta=u/(2n-1), giving O(n^3 a^-2 u^-2 log(n/alpha)) attempts by this simple,
non-optimal construction. Known positive attempt-rate lower bounds convert
event counts to elapsed calibration time. If local widths grow with n, a may
be exponentially small; bounded local width and accessible update attempts
must be part of the claimed polynomial regime.

parameter accuracy O(epsilon/n), not exponentially small accuracy.
